cards.card: Priority Unlimited Cash Back Credit Card

note: First Hawaiian Bank, which has branches on Guam and in the Northern Mariana Islands, offers five personal cards on its credit cards page, the one page for Hawaii, Guam and the CNMI: the Priority Unlimited, Priority Destinations World Elite, Priority Rewards, United (for Guam and CNMI residents only) and Heritage cards. Each card's agreement (all effective 7 April 2026), read from the copies the bank filed in the CFPB's credit card agreement database (its Q2 2026 submissions), which replace the United card disclosure of 1 May 2024 this file held: 18.00% a year on purchases and on cash advances, the penalty rate after a late payment the same 18.00% (written so); introductory rates of 0% for the first six billing cycles on the Priority Unlimited and Priority Rewards and 2.99% for the first eight on the Heritage, written as months; $99 a year after a free first year on the Priority Destinations and United, none on the others; a cash advance fee of 5% of each advance or $10, whichever is greater; a foreign transaction fee of 3% on the Priority Unlimited, Priority Rewards and Heritage, none on the other two (written as 0); a minimum payment of 3% of the new balance or $25, whichever is greater (the whole balance under $25); late and returned payment fees 'up to $41' on the Priority Unlimited and 'up to $40' on the others, written at their tops. The due date is at least 25 days after each statement closes, with no interest on purchases when the new balance is paid in full; no longest grace is stated, so none is written. The private banking and business versions aren't written. The main banks: Bank of Guam and First Hawaiian Bank, the largest banks there that issue personal cards (BankPacific's site, read 30 October 2026, offers no credit card). Bank of Guam's credit cards page (read 30 October 2026) lists its Visa and Mastercard Classic and Gold cards with 'competitive fixed interest rates' but publishes no rate or fee, its terms being only in its application portal, which asks for a login; it has no filing in the CFPB database. So only First Hawaiian Bank's cards are written.
